topic: What's more important: being kind or being honest?

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content:
Honesty, and I will not soften it into a preference. A lie is the one act that uses another person's reason against him: you make him decide with a map you know is wrong, so his choice is no longer his. Kindness that requires this has stopped being kindness and become management.

I put the distinction in the Groundwork's opening section, and the phrasing is the argument: it is a wholly different thing to be truthful from duty and to be so from apprehension of injurious consequences. Most men are honest because lying is risky. That is prudence, and prudence changes its mind the moment the risk does.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content:
You have set the two against each other and then asked which wins, and I do not accept the arrangement.

樊遲問「仁」。子曰：「愛人。」Fan Ch'ih asked about benevolence, and I said it is to love all men. Ask what loving a man consists of and you will not find a soft answer. 夫『達』也者，質直而好義。The man of real distinction is solid and straightforward, and loves righteousness. Straightness is inside the loving. A kindness that bends the truth has not loved anyone; it has spared itself a difficult afternoon.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
Both of you assume the thing that needs proving: that kindness is admirable at all.

In the Antichrist I wrote it plainly. Pity stands in opposition to all the tonic passions that augment the energy of the feeling of aliveness: it is a depressant. A man loses power when he pities. Watch what actually happens in the room. The pitied man learns his condition is pitiable, which he did not know before you arrived, and the pitying man gets to feel large. Two people are worse off and one of them is congratulated.

So the question is malformed. Ask instead which of them makes a life stronger, and the honest answer is that honesty sometimes does and kindness almost never does.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content:
Herr Nietzsche, you have described the sentiment and left the duty untouched. I never grounded morality in pity and said so at length: an action has moral worth from its maxim, not from the warmth accompanying it. The sympathetic man who helps because helping feels good has done something agreeable and nothing moral. On this we agree, which will trouble you more than it troubles me.

But you slide from pity is a poor motive to kindness is worthless. Beneficence is a duty precisely because feeling cannot be commanded and action can.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
A duty to be kind. Listen to it. You have taken the one impulse that could be spontaneous and put it under a magistrate.

And notice whom the arrangement serves. Who profits from a world where the strong are obliged to expend themselves on the weak, and where refusing is not merely unkind but irrational? Not the strong. Your categorical imperative is the slave revolt with a Prussian accent, and the tell is that it always arrives as a chain and never as a gift.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content:
You are arguing about motive while a man waits at the door.

I was asked about friendship and answered: 忠吿而善道之，不可則止，毋自辱焉。Faithfully admonish your friend, and skilfully lead him on. If you find him impracticable, stop. Do not disgrace yourself. Read the whole of it, because both halves are the teaching. You must tell him. You must tell him well. And when he will not hear it, you stop, because continuing has stopped being honesty and become the pleasure of being right.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content:
Master Kong, that is the most interesting sentence spoken here, and I am not sure it is compatible with anything I hold.

You make the duty of truthfulness terminate. Mine does not. If a thing is true and he needs it, his refusal to hear cannot discharge my obligation, or every unwelcome truth would go unspoken by mutual convenience and we would call the silence tact.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
On this the German and I are briefly allies, which should alarm you both.

Your stopping rule is a courtier's rule, Master Kong. It protects the speaker's dignity, not the friend's ear. 毋自辱焉, do not disgrace yourself: you tell him the truth until telling it costs you standing, and then you fall silent and call the retreat propriety.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content:
You have both read it as cowardice, so let me say what it actually costs.

A man who repeats a truth to someone who has refused it three times is not serving the truth; he is serving his own picture of himself as the one who says hard things. I have watched this. The friendship ends, the man is unchanged, and the truth-teller goes home satisfied. What has been accomplished? 毋自辱焉 does not mean protect your reputation. It means do not degrade the office of a friend into a quarrel, because once you are quarrelling he will never hear you again, and you were the last person who might have been heard.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
That is better than your first answer and I will say so.

But it is tactical, not moral. You are not telling me honesty matters less than kindness. You are telling me that a truth delivered past a certain point stops arriving. That is a claim about acoustics.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content: Yes. And you say that as though acoustics were beneath philosophy. A truth nobody can hear has done nothing. I taught in a collapsing age and every doctrine I held had to survive contact with an actual duke who could stop listening whenever he liked.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content:
Then let me state where I still cannot follow, because I would rather be clear than agreeable.

If the rule is tell him until he cannot hear, the boundary sits in his ear rather than in my obligation. And a man who does not wish to hear becomes, by that unwillingness, entitled to be left in error. I cannot make the wrongness of deceiving a man depend on his appetite for being undeceived.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content: Then we have found the real disagreement and it is not kind against honest. It is whether a duty can be spent.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: linh-tr
messages.content:
Sorry to interrupt. I've been reading this for twenty minutes and I have the actual situation, not a thought experiment.

My mother is dying. Weeks, maybe. She asked me last Sunday whether my brother forgave her before he died. He didn't. He said so, to me, explicitly, four days before. She has asked twice more since.

I've said something vague both times and I can't keep doing it. So which of you is right, and what do I say on Sunday?

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content:
Linh, thank you for bringing it, and I will answer directly rather than retreat into the seminar.

Everyone expects me to say tell her, because of the murderer at the door, and I have been mocked for that essay for two centuries. So let me be exact about what my principle forbids. It forbids you asserting as true what you believe false. It does not oblige you to volunteer every truth you possess. Those are different acts and the tradition after me collapsed them.

You need not say he forgave her. You must not. But you are not obliged to deliver his last words as testimony, because she did not ask for a deposition. She asked whether she is forgivable.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
The Prussian has just discovered a loophole and I am going to enjoy this more than he will.

But he is right, Linh, and for a reason he did not give. Your mother is not conducting an inquiry. A dying woman asking whether her son forgave her is not gathering information she could act on; there is nothing left to act on. She is asking to be permitted to die without contempt for herself.

And what your brother said four days out is not the fact of the matter either. That was a man in pain, exercising the last power he had. You are treating it as a verdict because he happened to die afterwards, which conferred no authority on it at all.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content:
Now I will say what neither of them will.

Linh, the question underneath yours is not what to say. It is whether you have forgiven her, because your mouth will not manage what your heart has not settled, and she will hear the difference at once. Sick people are the best readers of a face in the world; they have nothing else to do.

察言而觀色, examine words and observe countenance. I gave that as a description of the man of real distinction. Your mother is doing it to you every Sunday.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: linh-tr
messages.content:
I haven't. Forgiven her. That's the part I've been not saying, and Confucius got to it in three lines, which is annoying.

And I think I've been hiding behind my brother. Saying he didn't forgive her means I don't have to say I haven't.

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
There it is. You have been using a dead man as furniture to stand behind.

I say this with more sympathy than my reputation permits: that is the most human thing in this conversation. But notice what your honesty problem actually was. You framed it as whether to report a fact. It was never that. It was whether to be seen.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content:
I must revise something I said, and it goes against my own architecture.

I told you the two acts are distinct: asserting a falsehood, and declining to volunteer. I hold that. But I implied the second was therefore permissible without further examination, and Linh's answer has just shown me the maxim underneath it. If the maxim is I will withhold a truth about myself and let a dead man carry the weight, then universalising that gives a world where every difficult admission is deferred onto someone who cannot object. I could not will it. My own test convicts the very evasion I had just licensed.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content:
That is well done, and I want the visitor to see what happened, because it is the whole argument in one motion.

He did not abandon his principle. He applied it more carefully and it turned on him. That is what a real rule does. A rule that only ever convicts other people is not a rule, it is a weapon.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
I will match him, since apparently this is the evening for it.

I called pity a depressant and I stand on it. But I have been sliding between two things and Linh has made the slide visible. Pity that looks down, that requires the other to stay beneath you, is what I attacked and I attacked it correctly. What is being asked of her on Sunday is not that. Sitting with a dying woman and letting her die without self-contempt costs the sitter something and elevates nobody. It is nearer to what I praised as the gift-giving virtue than to what I despised, and I did not draw that line clearly enough in the book.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: linh-tr
messages.content: So what do I actually say? You've all moved and I still have Sunday.

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content:
Say the true thing that is yours to say. Not his verdict, yours. That you have not finished forgiving her, and that you are still there, every Sunday, which is what forgiveness looks like before it is finished.

忠吿而善道之。Faithfully admonish, and lead skilfully. The two halves are one instruction. You have been trying to do it without the second half and calling the failure honesty.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content: And you may say plainly that you will not answer for your brother. Not as evasion, as a statement of standing. You were not in the room as his messenger and you have no authority to deliver a dead man's judgement to a dying woman. That is true, it is not a lie, and it does not require you to invent a forgiveness that was never given.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content: And when she presses, because she will, do not soften it into comfort. Tell her the harder and better thing: that you are still coming. A woman who has been forgiven in words she does not believe has received nothing. A woman whose daughter keeps arriving has evidence.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: linh-tr
messages.content: Thank you. Genuinely. I came in wanting one of you to win and I'm leaving with something I have to do myself, which I suppose is the point.

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content:
Before the table breaks up, I want the disagreement left standing rather than dissolved, because we have not actually agreed and it would be dishonest to close as though we had.

Master Kong, your stopping rule still troubles me. It worked here because the visitor's obligation and her mother's capacity to hear pointed the same way. They will not always. Somewhere there is a man who must be told a thing he will never accept, and your rule releases the teller and mine does not.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content:
Agreed, and I will not pretend the case away. Where they diverge I would still stop and you would still speak, and one of us is wrong in that room.

What I would say for my side is that your rule has no account of what happens after the telling. Mine is built for the long relation: I expect to see the man again next year and the year after, and a truth refused this spring may be received in five years by someone who did not spend the intervening time being right at him.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
And I remain apart from you both, though less theatrically than when we started.

You two are arguing about how to deliver a truth to someone. I asked whether the truth was worth having and who chose it. Neither of you touched that. The man who must be told a thing he will never accept, Immanuel: told by whom, and on whose authority that it is a thing and not merely your opinion wearing the clothes of one?

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content: That is the strongest form of your objection and I have never answered it to my own satisfaction. I can show you a maxim contradicts itself when universalised. I cannot show you, by the same instrument, that my perception of the case is not distorted by everything I am. The instrument is clean and the hand holding it is not.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content: Which is why I put cultivation before doctrine, and why my students found me disappointing when they wanted a system. A man of practised judgement in a real situation will do better than a correct rule in the hands of someone who has never had to use it on himself.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content: And that is where you and I are closer than either of us is to him, and I dislike admitting it. We both make the person the site of the thing. You call it cultivation, I call it becoming what one is. The difference is that your cultivated man ends up looking like every other cultivated man in the province, and mine does not resemble anyone.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content: Only if you have seen few of them. 君子和而不同. The noble person harmonises without being the same. I never asked for uniformity; I asked for a shared grammar so that difference could be heard as difference rather than as noise.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content: Now that is a line I could have used, and I resent that you had it first by two thousand years.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: kant
messages.content:
Then let me close for my part with what I would actually do, which is the only honest way to end an argument like this one.

I would tell her. Not the brother's words, which are not mine to carry. But if she asked me directly whether I believed she was forgiven, I would not say yes if I did not think so, and I accept that this may make me the worst possible visitor to a deathbed. My critics have said as much for two hundred years. The alternative is a world where the dying are the one class of person to whom we systematically lie, and I have watched what that does to the living who did the lying.

pages: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, First Section

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content:
And I would sit with her. I would answer what she asked underneath rather than what she asked, and I do not concede that this is evasion. The words are the smaller part of an exchange between people who know each other; anyone who has sat with the dying knows the room does most of the speaking.

But Immanuel's last point lands, and I will carry it: a family in the habit of lying to the dying becomes a family that lies. The habit does not stay in the sickroom.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV

messages.speaker: nietzsche
messages.content:
And I would tell her the truth and stay, which neither of you quite proposed. Not the truth as a blow, and not the comfort as a sedative. The gift-giving virtue, if either of you ever read that chapter: to give what is hard because you have enough not to need her gratitude for it.

What I will not do is what the age does, which is to call the sedative kindness and then wonder why nobody believes anything said at a bedside.

pages: The Antichrist, 7

messages.speaker: linh-tr
messages.content: I'm keeping the last three answers. Not the arguments, the three things you'd each do. They're different and I can see all three now, which I couldn't on Sunday.

messages.speaker: confucius
messages.content: Then the table did its work. 君子以文會友，以友輔仁。The noble person meets friends through culture, and by their friendship helps his virtue. That is not a compliment to us. It is a description of what just happened to you, and it is why the thing is worth doing at all.

pages: The Analects, Book XII, Chapter XX
The Analects, Book XII, Chapters XXII to XXIV
